From Text to Application: MeDo’s Infrastructure

Developed within the Baidu ecosystem, MeDo uses natural language processing capabilities to turn text commands into working web applications. Aiming to accelerate the process of creating MVPs (Minimum Viable Products) for startups and developers, the platform can automatically build and deploy frontend, backend, database, and integration layers.

The platform analyzes users’ descriptions such as “income and expense tracking tool” or “e-commerce storefront” and builds the required code structure. The system is not limited to just a chat interface; it also allows generated applications to be edited via the visual editor using drag-and-drop. Support is also available for regional ecosystems such as WeChat Mini Programs.

Technical Architecture and Agent-Based Structure

The main feature that sets MeDo apart from standard no-code tools is its agent-based architecture running in the background. The system breaks complex business logic such as user session management, payment flows, and inventory tracking into small task components. These tasks are processed automatically at the code, infrastructure, and integration levels.

The following features stand out for professional developers and technical teams:

  • GitHub Integration: Generated code can be transferred directly to GitHub.
  • Self-Hosting Option: Projects can be hosted on the user’s own infrastructure without remaining dependent on the platform.
  • High Performance: The documentation targets API response times under 100 milliseconds and 99.9% uptime.
  • Broad Integration Network: Support is provided for connections with more than 500 third-party services.

Pricing Model

The platform uses a flexible credit-based pricing model. During the launch period, entry-level packages offer high credit volume at low cost, while the system allows trials through daily free credit allocations. This structure provides a cost advantage, especially for product teams that need rapid prototyping.
